title: Attacking Shape Foundations
primarySkill: Establishing an effective attacking shape around the football.
objective: Develop players’ understanding of how to form and maintain a balanced attacking shape that provides forward, lateral and release options for the player in possession.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 40 metres long by 30 metres wide, divided into three horizontal zones.
equipment: Three marker poles or cone gates
setup:
Divide players into two attacking groups of equal size.
One group operates at a time while the other group observes or completes a separate ball-handling activity.
Place one starting player with the football at one end of the area.
Position three to five teammates ahead of the football across the width and depth of the area.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
No defenders are used initially.
Players must avoid standing in a straight horizontal or vertical line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The starting player begins with the football and scans the attacking shape ahead.
Teammates establish at least one forward option, one lateral option and one release option behind or beside the football.
The football is moved by kick or handball through the area while all players adjust their positions after every disposal.
The player who disposes must immediately move to create another support option rather than remaining stationary.
The group scores by carrying or disposing the football through the scoring gate without two attackers occupying the same running lane.
Players reset at the opposite end and repeat in the other direction.
After several repetitions, introduce a five-second limit for the player in possession.
Rotate the observing group into the activity.
coachingPoints: Create options in front of, beside and behind the player in possession.
Avoid forming a flat line across the ground.
Maintain enough separation for each player to remain a genuine disposal option.
Adjust immediately when the football changes position.
Communicate early using names, direction and available space.
The nearest player should provide quick support without crowding the ball carrier.
Players further from the football should maintain width and depth.
Continue moving after disposing of the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players establish multiple disposal angles before the ball carrier comes under pressure.
Whether players maintain width and depth rather than following the football.
Whether the disposer moves again after releasing the football.
Whether players communicate before the football arrives.
Whether the attacking shape adjusts as possession moves through each zone.
Whether players can identify when the shape has become too flat or congested.

commonErrors.error: All players move towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold wider players in their lanes and require one player to remain ahead of the football.

commonErrors.error: Players form a straight line across the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger starting positions so each player is at a different depth.

commonErrors.error: The disposer stops after releasing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Require the disposer to run past, support behind or replace another player’s position.

commonErrors.error: Players call for the football after the ball carrier has already committed.
commonErrors.correction: Demand earlier communication and scanning before possession is received.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand too close together.
commonErrors.correction: Use cones to identify minimum spacing until players recognise the required distance.

progressions: Add one passive defender who applies shadow pressure to the player in possession.
Add a second defender who attempts to close the most obvious passing lane.
Require the group to use both sides of the area before scoring.
Introduce a turnover consequence if two attackers occupy the same lane.
Allow defenders to become fully active once the attacking shape is consistently maintained.
regressions: Use handball only over a smaller area.
Mark fixed starting positions for forward, lateral and release options.
Pause after each disposal and allow the coach to reposition players.
successIndicators: Provide at least three different disposal angles.
Move immediately after disposing of the football.
Reach the scoring gate without the shape collapsing around the ball carrier.
matchApplication: The drill introduces the basic attacking structure required whenever a team wins possession. Effective teams provide the ball carrier with options ahead of the football, across the ground and behind the contest. Maintaining this shape reduces congestion, improves possession retention and allows the team to move the football towards goal without relying on a single predictable option.
relatedDrills: DM-100 – Decision Making Chapter Final Assessment

title: Contact and Release Chain
primarySkill: Maintaining an attacking disposal chain through controlled contact.
objective: Teach players to remain composed through controlled contact and release possession to connected support without losing attacking momentum.
groundSize: A 35-metre-long by 20-metre-wide channel with three contact stations.
setup:
Mark three staggered contact stations through the channel.
Position one defender or pad holder at each station.
Divide attackers into groups of four.
Begin the football with the first attacker.
Position support runners behind and beside possession.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
Rotate contact roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first attacker carries towards the opening contact station.
The defender applies controlled body pressure.
The ball carrier protects possession and releases to a support runner.
The receiver continues towards the next contact station.
The previous disposer follows and becomes the next support option.
The sequence repeats through all three stations.
Support players must remain on different angles.
The group scores by reaching the final gate without a fumble or turnover.
Defenders may increase pressure gradually as technique improves.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Lower the centre of gravity before contact.
Keep the football away from the defender.
Maintain balance through the contact.
Release before the tackle becomes complete.
Support players should remain visible.
The disposer must continue running.
Communicate the next support option early.
Avoid blind or backward handballs.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier braces safely.
Whether possession remains protected.
Whether support players maintain clear angles.
Whether the release occurs before control is lost.
Whether the disposer follows the football.
Whether technique remains composed under repeated contact.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier holds the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Encourage earlier recognition and release.

commonErrors.error: Support runners move directly behind possession.
commonErrors.correction: Create angled support lanes.

commonErrors.error: The football is exposed to the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Carry on the protected side and use the body as a shield.

commonErrors.error: The disposer stops after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate follow-up running.

commonErrors.error: Players rush the handball before balance is established.
commonErrors.correction: Secure footing and control before release.

progressions: Replace pads with controlled live defenders.
Add a second defender at the final station.
Reduce the distance between stations.
Require players to choose between two support options.
Continue into a live scoring action.
successIndicators: Maintain execution across repeated contact efforts.
matchApplication: Attacking possession frequently continues through tackles, bumps and body pressure. Players must protect the football and release to support before the defence can create a stoppage or turnover.
relatedDrills: TK-120 – Tackling and Pressure Chapter Final Assessment
TO-013 – Numbers at the Contest Exit

title: Smother Recovery Connection
primarySkill: Recovering and reconnecting after an attacking disposal is smothered.
objective: Teach players to react immediately to a smothered kick or handball and create a connected second attacking possession.
groundSize: A 35-metre-long by 25-metre-wide area with a disposal zone and two recovery lanes.
setup:
Position one ball carrier inside the disposal zone.
Position one defender close enough to pressure or smother.
Place two attacking support players in separate recovery lanes.
Position one additional defender beyond the zone.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
The initial defender alternates between allowing the disposal and attempting a controlled smother.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives and prepares to dispose.
The defender applies immediate pressure and may attempt a controlled smother.
Support players remain active on separate angles.
If the disposal clears the defender, play continues towards the scoring gate.
If the football is smothered, the ball carrier and support players react immediately.
The nearest attacker attempts to recover the loose football.
Other attackers provide outside and rear support.
The second defender applies pressure to the recovery possession.
Attackers score two points for recovering the smother and reaching the gate.
Defenders score by winning the loose football and exiting through a side gate.
Reset after each outcome.
coachingPoints: Expect pressure on the disposal.
Support should remain active until the football clears the contest.
The original disposer must react immediately to the smother.
One player attacks the loose football while others spread.
Protect the recovery possession before releasing.
Avoid repeating the same blocked disposal line.
Use the recovery to change the attacking angle.
Apply pressure immediately if defenders win the loose football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether support players stop when the disposal begins.
Whether the original disposer reacts after the smother.
Whether one attacker takes responsibility for recovery.
Whether support forms on different angles.
Whether the next disposal avoids the original pressure line.
Whether defensive possession is pressured.

commonErrors.error: Players assume the disposal will clear the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain active support until the football is safely released.

commonErrors.error: The original disposer stands still after the smother.
commonErrors.correction: Demand an immediate second effort.

commonErrors.error: Several attackers collide at the loose football.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate the nearest player to recover while others spread.

commonErrors.error: The recovery disposal follows the same blocked path.
commonErrors.correction: Change the angle through lateral or rear support.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stop if defenders recover first.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and prevent the exit.

progressions: Make the smother defender fully active.
Add another recovery defender.
Reduce the area.
Continue into a live scoring phase.
Add repeated smother and spoil scenarios.
regressions: Predetermine whether the disposal will be smothered.
matchApplication: Smothers create unpredictable loose footballs and rapid changes in advantage. Teams that react first and remain connected can recover the possession and continue attacking before defenders reorganise.

title: Centre-Bounce Scoring Chain
primarySkill: Converting centre-bounce possession into a coordinated scoring opportunity.
objective: Develop a complete attacking chain from centre-bounce possession through midfield exit, forward connection and scoring-method selection.
groundSize: Centre square to the attacking goal using full forward-half width.
setup:
Use realistic centre-bounce numbers.
Position rucks and midfielders inside the centre square.
Position wings outside the square.
Position forwards and defenders in normal attacking-half roles.
Use normal goals.
Begin every repetition with a centre bounce or controlled ball-up.
Assign one team as the primary attacking team for three repetitions before rotating.
Allow legal match-like contact appropriate to the playing group.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin with a centre bounce.
Midfielders compete to win or receive the stoppage possession.
As possession is secured, attacking midfielders spread into forward, lateral and release lanes.
Wings adjust according to the exit side.
Forwards coordinate short, deep and clearing leads.
The ball carrier selects a direct entry, high-forward connection, handball surge or reset.
Play continues until a score, turnover or defensive exit.
Normal match scoring applies.
Award one bonus point for a clean centre-bounce exit.
Award another bonus point when the exit creates a controlled scoring opportunity.
If defenders win possession, they counterattack towards the opposite end gate.
Reset immediately for the next centre bounce.
Rotate ruck, midfield and forward roles after each block.
coachingPoints: Establish the intended exit before the bounce without becoming predictable.
Spread immediately after possession is won.
Wings must react to the actual exit rather than pre-empt it.
Forwards should coordinate movement with the midfield possession.
Protect the first possession before forcing an entry.
Use the high-forward connection when the direct route is covered.
Maintain support behind the ball carrier.
React immediately if the opposition wins the stoppage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether midfielders create separate exit lanes.
Whether wings adjust to possession direction.
Whether forwards time their leads correctly.
Whether the ball carrier has multiple entry choices.
Whether the team maintains support behind possession.
Whether the attack creates a quality shot rather than a rushed entry.
Whether transition response is immediate after a lost stoppage.

commonErrors.error: Midfielders remain clustered after the stoppage win.
commonErrors.correction: Assign forward, lateral and release spread responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Wings commit before possession direction is clear.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and react to the actual exit.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead before midfield control is established.
commonErrors.correction: Trigger movement when the first possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: The first ball carrier kicks blindly inside 50.
commonErrors.correction: Use the high-forward or release option when the direct entry is covered.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after a lost centre bounce.
commonErrors.correction: Make defensive transition part of the scoring system.

progressions: Change centre-bounce match-ups and structures.
Begin with the attacking team trailing late in the match.
Add a required scoring time limit.
Allow full-ground transition after turnovers.
Remove all coach communication during the repetition.
regressions: Pause after the stoppage win to organise spread.
matchApplication: Centre-bounce wins provide valuable scoring opportunities because both teams begin in structured positions. The advantage depends on clean exit, rapid spread and coordinated movement before the opposition can establish defensive support.
relatedDrills: RK-080 – Ruck and Stoppage Craft Chapter Final Assessment

title: Protect Lead and Counterattack
primarySkill: Protecting a late lead while remaining ready to counterattack.
objective: Teach players to retain possession and protect field position while recognising opportunities to counterattack and extend a late-game lead.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Set one team between one and twelve points ahead.
Set the clock between two and four minutes.
Begin the leading team in possession from varied field positions.
Use normal rules, boundaries and scoring.
Nominate time and field-position leaders.
The trailing team applies aggressive pressure.
Repeat with different leads and starting positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The leading team begins in possession.
Players assess whether to retain, advance, score or use the boundary.
The team maintains width and support behind possession.
If the opposition overcommits, attackers may launch a counterattack.
A counterattack should be taken only when the scoring chance is clear and turnover protection remains.
Turnovers are played live.
The scenario ends when time expires or the trailing team takes the lead.
Reset with a different score, time and field position.
Rotate leadership roles.
Coaches record risk decisions without interrupting play.
Review selected decisions.
Repeat the scenario under greater pressure.
coachingPoints: Know the score and remaining time.
Maintain active possession rather than standing still.
Use safe width, rear support and boundary positions.
Avoid unnecessary central turnovers.
Recognise when aggressive opposition pressure creates counterattacking space.
Counterattack with enough support to protect possession.
Take a clear score that extends the lead.
Maintain defensive balance behind every attacking action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether possession remains active and connected.
Whether players choose suitable field positions.
Whether the team becomes excessively defensive.
Whether counterattacking opportunities are recognised.
Whether enough players support the counterattack.
Whether defensive balance remains behind possession.
Whether scoreboard communication is accurate.

commonErrors.error: Players refuse every forward option.
commonErrors.correction: Take clear opportunities that extend the lead without excessive risk.

commonErrors.error: The team attacks centrally despite scoreboard control.
commonErrors.correction: Use safer width or boundary possession unless the central option is clearly open.

commonErrors.error: Players become stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Continue providing safe leads and replacement movement.

commonErrors.error: Too many players join the counterattack.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain defenders and rear support behind possession.

commonErrors.error: A counterattack begins without a genuine advantage.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until the defence overcommits.

progressions: Reduce the lead.
Increase opposition pressure.
Remove time reminders.
Begin from a defensive-half turnover.
Run repeated scenarios with limited recovery.
regressions: Give the leading team a numerical advantage.
Pause after turnovers to assess risk.
successIndicators: Preserve defensive balance until time expires.
matchApplication: Protecting a lead does not require abandoning attack. Effective teams control possession, manage field position and punish opposition overcommitment without exposing themselves to unnecessary turnover risk.
relatedDrills: TO-015 – Fast or Control Tempo Game

title: Rotating Match Scenario Circuit
primarySkill: Applying team offence across varied match scenarios.
objective: Prepare players to adapt their attacking method across a sequence of realistic match scenarios without losing the core principles of width, depth, connection and support.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare scenario cards including:
Centre-bounce attack.
Kick-in to score.
Defensive turnover transition.
Boundary pressure escape.
Forward-half repeat entry.
Two-minute comeback.
Protecting a late lead.
Wet-weather possession.
Reduced-bench fatigue.
Attack against a changing defensive system.
Use normal match rules and scoring.
Assign line leaders and scoreboard communicators.
Rotate the starting scenario every four to six minutes.
Allow appropriate recovery and safety adjustment between high-load blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Draw or select the first scenario.
Position players according to the match situation.
Begin live play.
The attacking team must identify the problem and select an appropriate method.
The defensive team applies realistic pressure and transitions after turnovers.
Normal scoring applies unless the scenario card provides a specific target.
Coaches assess attacking shape, decision quality, communication and outcome.
End the block when the scenario is completed or the nominated time expires.
Provide only brief feedback.
Select a different scenario.
Rotate leadership and specialist roles.
Complete the final two scenarios without coach feedback.
Finish with one unpredictable scenario selected during live play.
coachingPoints: Preserve width, depth and support in every scenario.
Identify the specific match problem quickly.
Select a method suited to score, time, field position and defence.
Communicate the plan across all three lines.
Adapt when the first option is removed.
Maintain possession quality under urgency.
Protect the team behind the football.
Apply immediate transition pressure after turnovers.
Retain core attacking principles when conditions change.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly players understand each scenario.
Whether line leaders organise the team.
Whether the selected method suits the match problem.
Whether players adapt after the first option closes.
Whether scoreboard and time awareness influence decisions.
Whether attacking structure remains connected.
Whether transition response is immediate.
Whether performance standards survive repeated scenario changes.

commonErrors.error: Players use the previous scenario’s method in the new situation.
commonErrors.correction: Reassess score, time, field position and defensive structure before restarting.

commonErrors.error: Communication remains local.
commonErrors.correction: Use line leaders to relay the attacking plan across the ground.

commonErrors.error: Urgency causes loss of shape.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width, depth and rear support while increasing decision speed.

commonErrors.error: Players become overly cautious after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish possession and attack the available opportunity.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue reduces tactical awareness.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the block and restore communication and positioning standards.

commonErrors.error: Core principles disappear when conditions change.
commonErrors.correction: Rebuild around connection, spacing and support before adding tactical detail.

progressions: Select scenarios without warning.
Change the defensive system during each block.
Reduce recovery between scenarios where safe.
Add numerical disadvantages.
Complete an extended final scenario under full match conditions.
regressions: Announce scenarios before players take position.
Provide the attacking team with a numerical advantage.
Pause midway through each scenario for correction.
successIndicators: Maintain width, depth and rear support.
Manage score, time and field position.
matchApplication: Teams must apply their attacking system in many different match situations. This circuit tests whether players can retain core offence principles while adapting tactics to score, time, field position, conditions and opposition structure.

title: Team Offence Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Applying the complete team-offence system under match conditions.
objective: Assess whether players can independently establish, maintain and adapt complete team offence from possession win through ball movement, forward entry, scoring and turnover response.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams using normal match positions.
Use full-ground dimensions and normal scoring.
Appoint defensive, midfield and forward leaders for both teams.
Prepare varied restarts and scenarios including:
Centre bounce.
Kick-in.
Defensive-half turnover.
Boundary pressure.
Forward-half repeat entry.
Late-game comeback.
Late-game lead protection.
Changing defensive system.
Wet-weather or difficult-ball simulation.
Reduced-rotation fatigue.
Assign coaches to assess separate components of team offence.
Use legal match-like contact appropriate to the playing group.
Provide no tactical coaching during the opening and final blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin with a standard match restart.
Teams play under normal rules for an opening assessment block.
The team in possession must establish width, depth and support ahead, beside and behind the football.
Players select the appropriate route through the ground.
Forwards coordinate scoring threats and entry movement.
Turnovers are played live with immediate transition.
After the opening block, introduce selected match scenarios.
Each scenario continues until a score, turnover, stoppage outcome or time limit.
Normal match scoring applies.
Coaches also record assessment points for:
Establishing attacking shape.
Providing multiple disposal options.
Escaping pressure cleanly.
Advancing all three playing lines.
Using width, corridor, switch and reset appropriately.
Creating and using numerical advantages.
Selecting an effective forward-entry method.
Maintaining two-way scoring threats.
Adapting to defensive systems.
Managing score and time.
Protecting against turnover.
Communicating across all lines.
Provide concise feedback between middle blocks only.
Rotate line leaders and selected positional roles.
Complete a final eight-to-ten-minute block under normal match rules.
Do not provide coach intervention during the final block.
Complete the assessment record after play ends.
coachingPoints: Establish attacking shape immediately after gaining possession.
Maintain width without losing connection.
Provide options at different depths.
Preserve support behind the football.
Select tempo according to numbers, space and pressure.
Use switches and resets to move defensive structures.
Access the corridor only when reward justifies risk.
Coordinate midfield and forward movement.
Maintain aerial and ground-level support.
Adapt to changing defensive systems.
Manage score, time and field position.
Communicate the attacking method across all three lines.
Protect the team against turnover.
Maintain standards under fatigue and match-like pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attacking shape forms without coach direction.
Whether the ball carrier consistently receives several options.
Whether width, depth and rear support remain connected.
Whether players away from the football maintain useful structure.
Whether pressure possessions are released cleanly.
Whether all three playing lines advance together.
Whether switches and resets create improved attacking pictures.
Whether corridor decisions are appropriately balanced.
Whether numerical advantages are identified and used.
Whether forwards coordinate short, deep, clearing and weak-side movement.
Whether scoring-method selection suits the defensive structure.
Whether players adapt to zone, press and man-on-man systems.
Whether scoreboard and time affect risk selection.
Whether leaders organise the team effectively.
Whether turnover protection and transition response are immediate.
Whether execution and decision quality survive fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd possession after winning the football.
commonErrors.correction: Restore forward, lateral, wide and rear support roles.

commonErrors.error: The team becomes flat across the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish staggered depth between playing lines.

commonErrors.error: Weak-side players follow the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold useful width and remain a genuine attacking threat.

commonErrors.error: Ball movement does not alter the defence.
commonErrors.correction: Change angle, tempo, depth or side with purpose.

commonErrors.error: Players force corridor possession.
commonErrors.correction: Assess receiver separation, next options and turnover consequence.

commonErrors.error: Switches finish with an isolated receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Move all three lines and provide forward, inside and rear support.

commonErrors.error: Forward entries become predictable.
commonErrors.correction: Use varied leading, running, contest and possession methods.

commonErrors.error: Numerical advantages become congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the free player outside defensive pressure.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to adapt to defensive changes.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the new system and select a collective response.

commonErrors.error: Scoreboard urgency causes reckless disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Increase decision speed without abandoning execution quality.

commonErrors.error: The team becomes passive while protecting a lead.
commonErrors.correction: Retain active possession and attack clear opportunities.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes loss of structure.
commonErrors.correction: Rotate roles and return to core spacing and connection principles.

commonErrors.error: Turnovers expose the team behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain defensive balance and immediate transition response.

progressions: Remove all scenario warnings and coach prompts.
Change defensive systems during open play.
Add score, time, field-position and numerical-disadvantage conditions.
Increase match-like contact where appropriate.
Complete an extended full-match simulation.
Use the assessment results to assign individual and line-specific development priorities.
regressions: Assess one phase of team offence at a time.
Provide the attacking team with a numerical advantage.
Pause between phases for structural feedback.
Shorten work blocks for younger, returning or masters players.
successIndicators: Maintain width, depth and rear support.
Advance defensive, midfield and forward lines together.
Use wing, corridor, switch, reset and overload options appropriately.
Coordinate forward movement and scoring threats.
Maintain decision quality and execution under fatigue.
Apply the complete team-offence system without constant coach direction.
matchApplication: This final assessment combines the complete Team Offence chapter from TO-001 to TO-099. It determines whether players can convert possession into organised, adaptable and efficient attack across technical, tactical, pressure, positional and match-scenario demands.
relatedDrills: TO-040 – Team Offence Running Patterns Assessment
TO-060 – Pressure and Contest Mastery Assessment
TO-080 – Team Ball Movement Final Assessment
